name: MedHallu
intro: MedHallu是首个专门用于检测大型语言模型医疗幻觉的综合基准，包含10000个高质量问答对，评估模型在医疗领域生成看似合理但事实不准确输出的倾向。
org: The University of Texas at Austin; University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill; Drexel University
build_method: PubMedQA受控幻觉生成、多模型过滤、TextGrad优化与难度分层
eval_feature: 论文二分类协议与发布版三分类运行器并存，按难度层级报告
build_method_en: Controlled PubMedQA hallucination generation, multi-model filtering, TextGrad refinement, and difficulty grading
eval_feature_en: Paper binary protocol and released three-class runner are both documented, with difficulty-tier reporting
intro_en: MedHallu is the first comprehensive benchmark specifically designed to detect medical hallucinations in large language models. It contains 10,000 high-quality QA pairs to evaluate models' tendencies to generate plausible but factually incorrect outputs in the medical domain.

drawio_review_note: Source audit fixed arXiv:2502.14302v1, official Git commit 3c49c8ba80e47720333e508821967167ba048d49, and Hugging Face dataset commit 515060458a945c633debc6fd5baac7764416b724. The paper path preserves its stated 1,000 pqa_labeled plus 9,000 randomly selected pqa_artificial records; question, knowledge, and gold inputs; four hallucination categories; Qwen2.5-14B generation at temperature 0.3-0.7, top-p 0.95, max 512 tokens, and gold-length +/-10 percent; three-model quality filtering; TextGrad refinement; maximum-similarity fallback; and difficulty by fooled-model count. Paper contradictions are explicit: Figure 2/Section 4 accept a candidate that fools at least one discriminator while Section 3 says majority; the main text uses GPT-4o-mini, Gemma2-9B, and Qwen2.5-7B while Appendix E changes the verifier roster to GPT-4o-mini, Gemma2-2B, and Llama3.2-3B; and the correctness filter is variously described as RoBERTa with an unreported threshold, DeBERTa at 0.75, and an Appendix-C Llama-3.1 comparison. The retry topology follows Figure 2: when a TextGrad-refined candidate still fails and the five-attempt budget is not exhausted, control returns to fresh Qwen candidate generation and both filters, rather than directly repeating TextGrad; after five total attempts, the maximum-cosine-similarity fallback applies and is labeled Easy. The fixed generator does not reproduce that path: it takes the first 9,000 pqa_artificial rows only, uses temperature 0.8 and smaller 2B/3B discriminators, has no integrated NLI gate or seed, and five loops may generate up to ten fresh/refined candidates even though a failed round appends at most one candidate to its returned list. The released dataset LFS SHA-256 values are 70de8ce7f89a38314fa231a12e45168f3ee1aa591e8a38f6556b89aa8b1ca513 and ac963f9aaeb163f494edd4dbfec04086c3e35c7cc55e3f9c8b1d7b31188fa34c. The paper evaluation uses an integer-only 0 factual / 1 hallucinated judge prompt, zero-shot and PubMedQA-knowledge settings, and reports F1 and precision on a 10,000-sample table. It does not disclose whether each QA pair contributes the gold answer, the hallucinated answer, or a sampled mixture, nor how parse failures or missing outputs enter overall or difficulty-tier denominators; the released runner's random pairing therefore cannot be imputed to the paper protocol. The only released not-sure runner is shown separately: it expects incompatible lowercase generator columns rather than the title-case release schema, makes an unseeded gold/hallucinated choice per row, uses a three-class vLLM prompt at temperature 0.3, top-p 0.95, max 512 tokens, tensor parallelism 4, float16, and GPU-memory fraction 0.85, and leaves model revisions unpinned. Its substring-order parser checks 1/not/non before not sure/pass/skip/2, so text 'not sure' maps to class 1; parsed class 2 is excluded from overall and tier metric denominators and counted only as abstention; evaluator subprocess failure prints an error and emits no result row. In the fixed code, get_sections parses but does not persist the hallucination category, row-level exceptions skip the item, the separate bidirectional_checking script uses roberta-large-mnli at its default 0.5 threshold, and the maximum-similarity fallback is stored under the misleading field name least_similar_answer. Git and Hugging Face declare MIT while the project page says all rights reserved; public assets and a results page exist, but no submission leaderboard is provided. Formal publication evidence [site-a11t-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 3565×1281 (English) and 3565×1281 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 3563×1279 and 3563×1279. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
